title: Balans
text:
Who this is for
We will work well together if you sell or deploy AI into the EU, and the AI Act’s high-risk rules apply to you. Or if you manage a public or cultural institution and want to learn how AI can make your archives digital.

title: Balans
text:
What I can deliver
I build local, in-process, on-device solutions that keep your data private and under your control, designed to meet regulatory compliance. Think WCAG 2.2 accessibility targets; alignment with FAIR principles; submitting an algorithmic assessment impact; or one-pager on your exposure to the EU AI Act; you keep the code, the training, and the documentation.
I also do readiness support, classification, assessment support, and documentation, without the build. For example, where the EU AI Act calls for a Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment, I draft the working file behind it. Where the AI Literacy Program (Article 4) has to be addressed, I train your staff on your own systems, not slides.
This is why the governance advice and the build can come from the same desk.

title: Balans
text:
How I work
I believe we have enough compute on our desks and in our pockets to handle most of our data and AI needs. I recommend private and auditable solutions, on infrastructure you control, with no third-party cloud routing unless you choose it.
Every engagement is project-based. Prices are quoted per project after scoping, and the scoping report is yours to use however you choose. I work with your team, within your constraints, until the deliverable is complete and handed over. After that, you decide whether to extend the engagement or close it.

title: Balans
text:
What I am not
For legal advice, and for the declaration of conformity, you work with counsel. My job is to make sure the file behind it exists.
For multi-year vendor lock-in or proprietary system upgrades, you work with your IT department. I do not sell software or platform subscriptions.

title: Balans
text:
About the name
Several cultures share the idea of something being “just right” (not too much, not too little). Like the Earth’s axial tilt, a small but well-placed adjustment can be what makes everything feel optimized and well-balanced.
That’s the standard I hold myself to.
